items.title: Ray Brown interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, AZ, April 16, 2000
items.q: He says, “You guys are the best musicians in the world, I’m paying you the best money, one take. Play what you want to hear.”

ctx.x: Norman Granz was a pretty important figure in jazz during those years. Was he a pretty upright guy to work for?

Oh yeah. You know he did a lot of brilliant things. First of all he put jazz into the concert hall. He took it out of the dance hall and put it in the concert hall. He took it out of the night club and put it in the concert hall. He gave people the very best musicians, I mean he got the top people, he always had top people playing for him, and he paid top salaries. I mean he was a tough guy. I remember we would finish a tour and it would be, we’d go in the studio and it would be Coleman Hawkins, Lester Young, Ben…
